The formal target uses h in {14,28,56}. A_i,h(t)=2/[h(h+1)] times sum from u=1..h of log(P_i[t+u]/P_i[t]); L_i is the equal one-third mean across the three horizons; M=L_SOL-L_ETH; Y=1 when M>0 and 0 when M<0; exact M=0 is TARGET_TIE and excluded from supervised scoring but counted.

Relative log-price z=log(SOL/ETH), daily relative log return d_t=z_t-z_{t-1}, and trailing relative volatility sigma240 is sample standard deviation ddof=1 over the most recent 240 d observations including t; epsilon is exactly 1e-12 where denominator protection is required.

The four primary momentum features are non-overlapping age buckets using d observations ending at t: K1=t-19..t length20, K2=t-59..t-20 length40, K3=t-119..t-60 length60, K4=t-239..t-120 length120. Each K=tanh(sum(d)/((sigma240+1e-12)*sqrt(block_length))); no cumulative FAST/SLOW or separate acceleration feature is added.
Persistence60 is the arithmetic mean of sign(d) over t-59..t. Exact zero relative returns contribute zero so asset exchange remains antisymmetric.
Position120 is 2*(z_t-min(z_t..z_t-119))/(max-min)-1 with exact zero range mapped to 0. This symmetric relative-position feature replaces the earlier non-antisymmetric relative-drawdown idea.

Participation uses Binance quote_volume only: Activity_i=log((median20_quote_volume_i+1e-12)/(median120_quote_volume_i+1e-12)); Participation=tanh(Activity_SOL-Activity_ETH). It is called relative participation, not capital flow or order flow.
The sole candidate feature vector is exactly [K1,K2,K3,K4,Persistence60,Position120,Participation], each naturally bounded in [-1,1]; no data-dependent z-score standardization is used.

At each refit, expanding Laplace-smoothed matured-label prevalence pi=(N_SOL+1)/(N_SOL+N_ETH+2) is a fixed causal prior. Candidate raw probability is sigmoid(logit(pi)+beta'X) with no fitted intercept. Ridge lambda is fixed at 1 and no hyperparameter search is allowed.
ETH/SOL exchange must map X to -X and pi to 1-pi, and therefore predicted probabilities must sum to one under asset-label exchange within numerical tolerance fixed by implementation tests.

A historical origin s can enter training at prediction origin t only when s+56 calendar days<=t and s was 0048-eligible. Training is expanding. The first shadow prediction requires at least 365 eligible feature-valid fully matured training origins.
Model refits occur every 28 calendar days from the first valid refit anchor. Between refits beta and the prevalence offset are frozen; predictions may be emitted only on eligible origins.

Calibration is shadow-prequential. A raw prediction is stored before its outcome exists and may enter the calibration pool only after its full 56-day label matures. Formal calibrated evaluation begins only after at least 365 matured eligible shadow prediction/outcome pairs exist.

Primary calibration preserves the prevalence prior: p_cal=sigmoid(logit(pi)+gamma*eta), eta=beta'X, gamma>=0 selected by calibration-pool NLL. If no finite stable minimizer exists, calibration is unidentified. Beta calibration and isotonic regression are diagnostics only with zero replacement or rescue authority.
For numerical NLL scoring only, probabilities are clipped to [1e-12,1-1e-12] after model/calibration computation; clipping has no effect on winner direction or confidence state.

B0 is uniform p=0.5. B1 is expanding Laplace prevalence pi. B2 is a one-feature lagged-leader model using H=sign(PastL_SOL-PastL_ETH), where PastA_i,h=2/[h(h+1)]*sum_{u=1..h}log(P_i[t]/P_i[t-u]) for h={14,28,56} and PastL is their equal-third mean. B3 is one-feature 60-day relative momentum RM60=tanh((z_t-z_t-60)/((sigma240+1e-12)*sqrt(60))).

B2 and B3 use the same expanding training, fixed ridge lambda=1, prevalence offset, 28-day refit and shadow-prequential prior-preserving calibration protocol as the candidate. AlwaysHistoricalFavorite is classification diagnostic only.

The simultaneous NLL gate computes d_b,t=loss_candidate-loss_baseline_b. For each 56-observation moving-block bootstrap replicate, aligned evaluation rows are resampled without retraining the walk-forward models. Let T*=max_b(mean(d_b*)-mean(d_b)); q95 is its 95th percentile. Simultaneous UCL_b=mean(d_b)+q95 and G2 requires max_b UCL_b<0.

Primary moving-block bootstrap uses block length 56 ordered eligible formal-evaluation observations, 10000 replicates and seed 4292549012. All candidate/baseline rows share identical sampled block indices. The final overrun is truncated to N.
Confidence is c=2*abs(p_cal-0.5). Direction-corrected realized margin is Z=sign(p_cal-0.5)*M. The confidence-strength curve is G(c)=E[Z|c].

G(c) shape diagnostic uses a natural cubic regression spline with boundary knots 0 and 1 and internal knots 0.25,0.50,0.75. No monotonic constraint or smoothing search is allowed. G' and G'' are diagnostics; argmax G'' has no threshold-selection authority.

The sole HIGH breakpoint model is G(c)=alpha+beta*c+delta*(c-kappa)_+ with exactly one breakpoint. Kappa is the deterministic global SSE minimizer over admissible kappa in [0.20,0.80], ties broken toward the smaller kappa. Each side must contain at least 10% of evaluation observations and at least 4 distinct full 56-observation blocks.

Each bootstrap replicate re-fits the spline and segmented breakpoint on its resampled evaluation rows. Reliable breakpoint requires at least 90% admissible bootstrap breakpoints, percentile 95% kappa CI width<=0.20, and delta>0 in at least 95% of valid breakpoint replicates.

G7 uses percentile 95% moving-block-bootstrap CI for Spearman(c,Z). G8 uses the bootstrap replicate's own admissible kappa to define its HIGH sample and forms the percentile 95% CI of HIGH mean Z, so breakpoint uncertainty is included.

Formal evaluation support requires at least 12 complete sequential 56-observation blocks. A trailing partial block enters aggregate metrics but not the support count. Each realized direction must appear in at least 3 distinct full blocks.

Formal evaluation is mechanically split into four contiguous equal-count temporal blocks with sizes differing by at most one. G5 requires candidate NLL below the minimum baseline NLL in at least 3 of 4 blocks.

Causal episodes are maximal contiguous eligible runs of the sign of Rrel60=log[(SOL_t/SOL_t-60)/(ETH_t/ETH_t-60)]. Exact zero inherits the prior nonzero state; an ineligible day terminates the episode. Only episodes of duration at least 14 calendar observations enter G6 equal-episode robustness.
G6 requires both median episode candidate-minus-best-baseline NLL<0 and strictly more than half eligible episodes with negative differential.

HIGH is c>=kappa only after G9 identifies a reliable breakpoint. If no reliable breakpoint exists, no daily HIGH state is authorized and concentration handoff fails while leadership prediction evidence may still pass.

G10 requires HIGH coverage>=10% and HIGH observations in at least 6 distinct full 56-observation blocks. G11 requires SOL-HIGH in at least 2 eligible causal SOL episodes and ETH-HIGH in at least 2 eligible causal ETH episodes.

Subsampling is a nonselection sign-robustness diagnostic only. Block length b=max(56,ceil(N^(2/3))); all contiguous overlapping subsamples are used; each subsample computes Dmax=max_b mean(d_b). If primary G2 passes but at least half of subsamples have Dmax>=0, report INFERENCE_FRAGILE. This diagnostic has no rescue authority.
